title: Adiabatic Variational Principle: Born-Oppenheimer Theory for Emergent Electronic-Order Dynamics
authors: Yang Yang, Ali Rayat, Ho Jang, Yunhao Fan, Sankha Subhra Bakshi, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: Recent advances in microscopic many-body methods have enabled increasingly accurate descriptions of equilibrium quantum states, yet large-scale simulations of emergent-order dynamics typically rely on phenomenological equations with prescribed free-energy functionals. We introduce the Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP), a framework for deriving order-parameter dynamics directly from an interacting many-body Hamiltonian. When microscopic relaxation is fast compared with order-parameter evolution, the many-body state follows the collective configuration adiabatically, in analogy with the Born--Oppenheimer separation of electronic and nuclear motion. This assumption makes explicit the adiabatic closure implicit in conventional phase-field descriptions. Each instantaneous order-parameter configuration then defines a constrained quasi-stationary many-body state, and the Lagrange multipliers enforcing these constraints directly provide the thermodynamic forces driving the collective evolution. Nonlinear Mori--Zwanzig projection theory further connects the reversible dynamics to the microscopic algebra of the collective variables and relates dissipation and fluctuations to the eliminated degrees of freedom. Applications to charge- and spin-density-wave dynamics recover Allen--Cahn domain growth, resolve evolving domain networks together with their microscopic electronic structure, and yield generalized Landau--Lifshitz dynamics for itinerant magnetism. The AVP thus provides a solver-independent microscopic foundation for phase-field-like simulations of the nonequilibrium dynamics of emergent electronic order.
summary: This paper introduces the Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP) to derive the dynamics of emergent electronic order directly from a full many-body Hamiltonian. By assuming fast electronic relaxation relative to slow order-parameter changes, it establishes a rigorous, microscopic foundation for phase-field simulations. This framework successfully reproduces known dynamics for CDW and magnetic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a microscopic foundation to simulate the non-equilibrium dynamics of emergent electronic order, bridging the gap between fundamental many-body theory and phenomenological phase-field models.
main_result: The Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP) successfully derives order-parameter dynamics directly from the interacting many-body Hamiltonian, providing a solver-independent framework for such simulations.
method: The core method is the Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP), which assumes the system evolves adiabatically with respect to slow order parameters, analogous to the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
model_or_system: The study applies to correlated quantum matter exhibiting emergent electronic order, such as charge-density waves (CDW) and itinerant magnetism, starting from an interacting many-body Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Order parameters ($\phi$), thermodynamic forces derived from Lagrange multipliers, and domain growth patterns (e.g., Allen-Cahn dynamics).
important_parameters: The separation of time scales ($	au_{qp} \ll 	au_{\phi}$) is crucial, defining the adiabatic limit.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that microscopic relaxation is fast compared to the evolution of the order parameter (adiabatic assumption), and the dynamics are treated in the Markovian limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the AVP, drawing an analogy to the Born-Oppenheimer separation where the slow order parameter defines a constrained microscopic state, and Lagrange multipliers provide the driving forces.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the AVP framework, details its connection to Born-Oppenheimer theory, derives the equations of motion using Mori-Zwanzig theory, and applies the formalism to recover known dynamics like Allen-Cahn and Landau-Lifshitz equations.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, microscopic derivation for dynamics often modeled phenomenologically in AMO and condensed matter, connecting slow collective variables to fast quantum fluctuations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP). In analogy with the Born–Oppenheimer separation of slow and fast degrees of freedom, a slowly evolving order-parameter field ϕ(r, t) defines, at each instant, a constrained microscopic many- body state ˆρ[ϕ]. Here, however, the slow variable is an emergent collective observable rather than an independent microscopic coordinate. The associated Lagrange multipliers provide the thermodynamic forces that drive the collective evolution, while the microscopic state follows the changing order-parameter configuration adiabatically.

FIG. 2. Schematic illustration of adiabatic dynamics based on the AVP. For a given instantaneous configuration of the slow order parameters, the constrained variational problem determines the corresponding adiabatic microscopic state and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The resulting state also provides the expectation values of microscopic observables characterizing the nonequilibrium system. The effective equa- tion of motion, including both reversible and dissipative con- tributions, then advances the order parameters to the next time step. Repeating these two steps generates the coupled evolution of the slow collective variables and the microscopic many-body state.

FIG. 3. Schematic of the MF-AVP workflow. For a pre- scribed order-parameter configuration ϕ, the inner loop deter- mines the single-particle density matrix G and the Lagrange multipliers f enforcing the constraints. The map F converts constraint residuals A[G] −ϕ into corrections to f and de- pends on the numerical implementation. At convergence, the multipliers provide the thermodynamic forces f = −∂F/∂ϕ used to advance ϕ in the outer dynamical loop.

FIG. 4. Coarsening dynamics of the charge-density-wave state in the square-lattice t–V model. The columns show snapshots at t = 0, 5, 10, and 40, with time measured in units of (Γtnn)−1, where Γ is the dissipative coefficient in Eq. (49). (a) Local checkerboard order parameter ϕi defined in Eq. (46), showing the formation and coarsening of domains whose opposite signs distinguish the two symmetry-related checkerboard states. (b) Conjugate thermodynamic force fi associated with the dynamical density variable ni. (c) Local density of states ρi near the Fermi energy, evaluated from the instantaneous constrained mean-field Hamiltonian.

FIG. 5. Dynamical scaling of square-lattice CDW coarsen- ing. The normalized equal-time correlation function C(r, t) of the staggered CDW field is plotted against r/L(t), where C(L(t), t) = 1/2. Correlations at different times collapse at short rescaled distances, with deviations at larger distances as finite-size effects become important. The inset shows the characteristic domain size L(t), whose growth is consistent with the Allen–Cahn law L(t) ∼t1/2 over the coarsening regime.
